Bug_Details:
computeIfAbsent passes the map key to the provided class's constructor With ambiguous constructor references used in java.util.Map#computeIfAbsent
function parameter, it becomes unclear what the code intends to do. map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() Code of this form can seemingly look like it’s trying to make a counter,
creating the key if absent. Unfortunately the code is surprising, because it
will call the wrong AtomicLong constructor. Instead, it will create the
counter initialized with the key value, which is probably not desired.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the line where the AtomicLong constructor is called with the parameter someLong. This creates an AtomicLong object with the initial value of someLong, which is not the intended behavior. The intended behavior is to create an AtomicLong object with the initial value of 0, which is the default behavior of the constructor.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases trigger the bug by creating an AtomicLong instance with an initial value, and then incrementing it using the incrementAndGet() method. This triggers the bug because the computeIfAbsent() method in the original code is called with an ambiguous constructor reference, causing the wrong AtomicLong constructor to be called.
